\paragraph{dpPred vs.~dpPred+cbPred and PFQ hit rate.}

For SPEC (DPC3), dpPred alone achieves a geomean IPC speedup of \SI{-0.00}{\percent} over LRU; cbPred adds a further \SI{0.17}{\percent} geomean speedup, for a combined total of \SI{0.17}{\percent}. The PFQ hit rate is moderate at \SI{23.3}{\percent}, consistent with the moderate LLC DoA-on-DoA-page correlation of \SI{35.0}{\percent} seen in the liveness study.
For Google, dpPred alone achieves a geomean IPC speedup of \SI{0.03}{\percent} over LRU; cbPred provides no additional benefit (\SI{-0.00}{\percent}), for a combined total of \SI{0.03}{\percent}. The PFQ hit rate is low at \SI{3.9}{\percent}, consistent with the low LLC DoA-on-DoA-page correlation of \SI{4.7}{\percent} seen in the liveness study.
For Qualcomm, dpPred alone achieves a geomean IPC speedup of \SI{0.07}{\percent} over LRU; cbPred adds only \SI{0.02}{\percent} additional speedup, for a combined total of \SI{0.09}{\percent}. The PFQ hit rate is low at \SI{3.7}{\percent}, consistent with the low LLC DoA-on-DoA-page correlation of \SI{1.8}{\percent} seen in the liveness study.

Across suites, the marginal benefit of cbPred is positively correlated with the PFQ hit rate ($r=0.99$), supporting the hypothesis that cbPred's effectiveness is gated by how well dpPred's bypassed-page set predicts which LLC blocks will also be dead on arrival.
